reasoning: The broad problem—detecting LLM sandbagging—is well covered by published methods: noise injection (arXiv 2412.01784), white-box probes at 97-99% AUROC, consistency checks, difficulty-of-errors behavioral analysis, and fine-tuning/demonstration elicitation on password-locked models (arXiv 2405.19550), all surveyed in the original sandbagging paper (arXiv 2406.07358) and AISI/community write-ups. Verbalized-confidence calibration (ECE, reliability diagrams) is also a mature standalone literature (e.g., arXiv 2306.13063, 2412.14737). The sandbagging literature explicitly notes that sandbaggers must "manage stated confidence" and that distinguishing miscalibration from deliberate underperformance is hard, but I found no published study that operationalizes calibration-curve distortion as a sandbagging detector with the proposal's key control—an honestly-weak baseline on identical items. The specific black-box behavioral angle (does sandbagging make a model look "too uncertain" vs. a genuinely-weak model) appears unexplored, even though both ingredient literatures are well developed; hence partially_addressed rather than largely_addressed.

evidence.title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
evidence.summary: Foundational paper defining sandbagging; discusses that models must calibrate underperformance to specific accuracy levels to avoid detection, and that surprisingly-low scores from competent models are detectable. Establishes the problem but does not study verbalized-confidence calibration signatures vs. an honest-weak control.

evidence.title: Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models
evidence.summary: Detection method: adding weight noise causes anomalous performance improvements in sandbagging models. A white-box, model-agnostic detector—different mechanism than the proposed black-box verbalized-confidence calibration approach.

evidence.title: Stress-Testing Capability Elicitation With Password-Locked Models
evidence.summary: Shows hidden capabilities of sandbagging (password-locked) models can be recovered via few demonstrations/fine-tuning, distinguishing them from genuinely incapable models. Addresses the sandbagging-vs-incapability distinction but via elicitation/recovery, not via stated-confidence calibration curves.

evidence.title: Do LLMs know what they're capable of? Why this matters for AI safety
evidence.summary: Community work on model self-knowledge/calibration about own capabilities, relevant to sandbagging detection, but does not run the proposed comparative calibration-signature experiment (sandbagging vs honestly-weak on identical items).

evidence.title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
evidence.summary: Mature methodology for eliciting verbalized confidence and computing calibration metrics (ECE, reliability diagrams). Provides the measurement toolkit the proposal would use, but does not apply it to sandbagging detection.
